title: Consolidate responsive button/table/chart variants and add publish CI gating
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: Reduce variant surface area for buttons, tables, and chart atoms to improve runtime publish stability and make auto-layout predictable across density breakpoints. We'll collapse rarely-used responsive variants into a smaller set of canonical variants, standardize auto-layout constraints for row/column atoms, align semantic tokens for spacing and typography, and add a CI gating step to fail library publishes when variant diffs exceed a threshold or introduce broken constraints. 

Scope and deliverables:
- Audit existing variants for Button, Table Row, Table Header, Chart Legend, Chart Point, and Compact/Comfortable density modes. Produce a CSV mapping old->canonical variants.
- Implement Figma library edits: rename canonical variants using the new naming pattern (component/state/density) and remove duplicates where behavior is identical within +/- 2px of measured layout.
- Normalize auto-layout on table row and chart legend components to explicit spacing tokens (spacing.xs, spacing.s, spacing.m). Replace mixed fixed padding with tokenized padding.
- Create migration alias components (deprecated variants) that render a redlined label in the inspector for one release before deletion.
- Add publish gating script integration: a Jenkins/CI job that calls Figma API to compute variant diff and constraint warnings; block publish if variant count delta > 15% or if any component has mixed axis constraints.
- Update documentation: Confluence guide, release notes, and quick migration cheat-sheet for engineers.

Acceptance criteria:
- Canonical variant set documented and approved by PM and Eng.
- No visual regressions in primary token combos for buttons/tables/charts (verified by Percy snapshots).
- CI gate prevents library publish when variant diff or broken constraints are detected.
- Migration aliases exist in the library for two release cycles with clear deprecation messaging.

Trade-offs and notes:
- We will remove low-usage density variants that add maintenance cost; this may require small layout tweaks in three consumer apps (alerts from dependency ENG-4218 indicate affected screens). We accept the manual update burden for those apps in exchange for long-term stability and smaller publish diffs.
- Using a strict numeric threshold for gating (15%) is conservative; we can relax after two weeks of telemetry if we see many false positives.
- The migration alias approach increases temporary clutter but preserves discoverability and reduces immediate breakage for teams that haven't migrated yet.

Rollout plan:
1) Audit and propose canonical mappings (this ticket). 2) Engineering partner implements publish CI hook (ENG-4218). 3) Design makes Figma edits in a feature branch and opens PR (link in attachments). 4) QA Percy snapshots + manual review. 5) Roll out migration aliases and notify workspace. 6) After one cycle, remove deprecated variants.

Stakeholders: UX Design (Maya Chen), Component Leads (Liam O'Donnell), PM (Arjun Patel), Frontend Eng (Sofia Martinez), Platform Eng (Nikhil Rao).
